product: Globemaster 12" Blue Ocean Desk Globe with Raised Relief

entries.text: Hi, it's Mia from Replogle Globes. Thanks for taking a few minutes with me: your code, $20 off, shows up on screen as soon as we finish. I see you were looking at the Globemaster 12" Blue Ocean Desk Globe with Raised Relief. What caught your eye?
Uh, probably the price.
Fair enough, it's $79. I should mention that this one shows as sold out right now. What would the globe be for?
Educational purposes for children.
That's a good use for it. Raised relief can help kids get a feel for mountains and land. Who's it for, and what did you hope it would do for them?
That's a gift for some friends' kids.
Nice, a thoughtful gift. When you give something like this to friends' kids, what do you hope happens once they've opened it?
Learn the position of different countries, locate themselves in the world, have a better sense of geometry and distances traveling, and learn basic navigation skills.
Navigation skills too, that's a great list. Are you comparing Replogle Globes with other stores or brands for this gift?
Yes. Comparing with couple other brands, but Replogo came highly recommended So my preference is Replagal.
Good to hear it came highly recommended. Who or where did you hear about Replogle Globes?
Online forums.
For teachers and educators and parents.
So the forums were full of teachers and parents, that's a trustworthy crowd. Have you given a gift like this before, and how did it go?
No. This will be the first globe that I'm purchasing for a gift. I haven't purchased any globes in the past before.
That makes this a special first. What do you usually give the kids in your life, and roughly what do you spend on a gift?

Well, I don't often gifts. I just have some new friends that have kids and looking for something. They did a favor for us, so we're just returning the favor with a gift. And... Yeah. So I wouldn't know what specifically I'd be looking for since I don't often buy gifts for kids.
That's a kind way to say thanks, and no pressure. Are there any monthly services or subscriptions you pay for, and what keeps you with them?
Like, in general monthly, subscriptions, like, for anything or related to, like, globes and maps?
Anything at all, whatever you pay for regularly. Which ones do you keep, and what makes them worth it to you?

I try not to pay for any I'm quite against the subscription model. I think that, uh, some services should be rendered as a of ownership rather than a continuing ongoing thing. But if I have to, generally, be at work related services, Yeah.
Owning rather than renting makes sense, and a globe fits that. What would feel like a fair amount to spend on this gift?

Oh, definitely under a hundred dollars, um, just because of the social dynamic, the situation, the appropriateness of expenditure, um, and the use case. With kids, I think that, uh, under a hundred dollars would probably be the most appropriate. Cheaper, the better without compromising quality.
Cheaper without compromising quality, that's clear, and thank you for being so open with me. Your code is coming up on your screen now. Goodbye!
